name: LiftFrozenFinger
summary: A MultiFingerBubble variant for dense scenes: clenching the fist freezes the hand-controlled bubble in place, and lifting the thumb, index or middle finger out of the fist selects the matching target inside it.
howItWorks: With the palm open, a transparent bubble follows the hand and captures up to three nearby targets, each coloured to match a finger in left-to-right order. Clenching the fist freezes the bubble (Single-Hand Frozen Gestures, SHFG), so further hand movement no longer changes which targets it holds, which prevents the last-second change of colours caused by the Heisenberg effect. Lifting the corresponding finger from the fist selects that target; opening the palm unfreezes the bubble to correct it. In a 16-participant study (Vive Pro with a Leap Motion) selecting small atoms in dense clusters, LiftFrozenFinger raised the success rate by 15.71% and PianoFrozenFinger by 34.29% over MultiFingerBubble, with less hand fatigue; both were slower than MultiFingerBubble, PianoFrozenFinger was more accurate than LiftFrozenFinger, and 12 of 16 participants ranked it first.
advantages: Freezing the bubble stops targets changing at the moment of selection.
Lifting a finger from a fist is easier to track and less tiring than bending fingers from an open hand.
limitations: Slower than MultiFingerBubble because of the extra fist step.
Only three fingers are used, so a bubble holds at most three targets.
Tested only on near targets in a molecule-like scene.

relationships.note: Adds the fist freeze and replaces bending fingers with lifting them.
Higher success rate and less fatigue, but slower.
PianoFrozenFinger was more accurate; times did not differ.

review.notes: Coded from the IJHCI full text. Motor-visual space follows the MultiFingerBubble entry (bubble moved by the palm); the targets sat about 50 cm to 1 m in front of the user. The paper does not address occlusion directly.
